$comment: Spells, artifacts and profile perks, rendered by rushroyale.js on spells.html. Sourced from the game's in-game Knowledge Base, recorded 2026-08-27, which is authoritative - these entries carry no 'detail' flag because they are not waiting on verification. What is missing here is the roster, not the rules: the in-game text explains how the system works without naming the individual spells, artifacts and relics, so none are invented. Only the six archetypes are recorded so far, as kind='Archetype'. When real spells and artifacts are added, give them kind='Spell', 'Artifact' or 'Relic' and the filter chips will appear on their own - buildChips() skips a facet with fewer than two distinct values. Fields as in resources.json: name, id (becomes the anchor), kind (the filter facet), summary, facts (ordered [label, text] pairs), tags. Authored order follows the order the game lists the archetypes in.

entries.name: Damage
entries.summary: The spells and artifacts that specialize in increasing the damage you deal.
facts: In PvP the number that counts is your hit on the Phantom at the end of a wave, because that is what becomes the boss on the other player's path.

entries.name: Economy
entries.summary: The spells and artifacts that specialize in granting extra mana, merge ranks or units.
facts: Gives you extra mana, extra merge ranks, or extra units.
Mana and board space are the two things a match is actually short of, so an economy effect buys everything else.

entries.name: Monsters
entries.summary: The spells and artifacts that specialize in making the opponent's monsters more powerful.
facts: Strengthens the monsters walking at your opponent.
PvP only in effect - co-op has no opponent to send anything to.

entries.name: Negatives
entries.summary: The spells and artifacts that specialize in weakening the opponent in various ways.
facts: Weakens the opposing player rather than strengthening you.
PvP only in effect, for the same reason as Monsters.

entries.name: Empowerment
entries.summary: The spells and artifacts that specialize in making the decks suited for special strategies stronger.
facts: Rewards a deck built around a particular strategy rather than a general-purpose one.
Decks with a specific plan. An empowerment effect attached to a strategy your deck does not run is a dead slot.

entries.name: Defense
entries.summary: The spells and artifacts that specialize in protecting your units against the various negative effects.
facts: Protects your units from negative effects.
The Negatives and Monsters archetypes on the other side of the board, and boss abilities that disable units.
